source.title: Artificial Neural Variability for Deep Learning: On Overfitting, Noise Memorization, and Catastrophic Forgetting
source.authors: Zeke Xie; Fengxiang He; Shaopeng Fu; Issei Sato; D. Tao; Masashi Sugiyama

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; figures are represented as flattened text and plot labels, without recoverable point values.
record.tranche_reason: Tests noisy-label memorization with experiments comparing standard SGD and a different optimizer, NVRM; it does not reproduce the original fully random-label experiment.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Zhang et al. (2017) for random-label fitting, but that cited result is not this study's evidence. Its own results vary label-noise rates and report training and test accuracy. Numerical curve values are figure-only.
record.test_reason: The study's SGD controls directly test noisy-label fitting using training accuracy, the same method and measure as the original experiments. These results bear on V4 despite the paper's emphasis on a new optimizer.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that NVRM reduces noisy-label memorization, with asymmetric-noise experiments described as SGD memorizing nearly all noisy labels while NVRM predominantly learns clean labels.
record.recipe_differences: Uses NVRM, which adds weight perturbations during training and removes them before inference; compares it with SGD and perturbed SGD. The label-noise experiments do not reproduce the original random-label settings.
record.method_sensitivity: Label-noise type and rate; dataset (CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100); optimizer (SGD, NVRM, or PSGD); NVRM noise type and scale.

fits_no_version.finding: Continual-learning accuracy on Permuted MNIST improves with NVRM.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: NVRM reduces forgetting across tasks with fixed pixel permutations; this does not establish V3's zero-training-error claim.

fits_no_version.finding: Larger stochastic gradient noise slows noisy-label memorization, but SGD eventually memorizes nearly all noisy labels.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimization settings affect memorization speed at a fixed corruption rate; this does not measure V2's dependence on corruption fraction.

record.problems: The noisy-label curves are presented as figures without recoverable numerical values in the supplied text. The experiments use selected corruption rates rather than the complete range from no noise to fully random labels. The paper reports 10 trials and standard deviations generally, but the relevant figure descriptions do not give numerical uncertainty.
record.rows_left_out: No rows extracted: the relevant training-accuracy curves in Figure 3 are figure-only in the supplied text, and the explicit prose is qualitative. Figure 10 reports test-accuracy curves for additional symmetric-noise rates but gives no recoverable point values or text describing the corresponding training accuracy.

untested.parts: Completely random labels, chance test accuracy, and fitting without changing architecture or training hyperparameters.
Training-time ratios for true versus random labels and convergence slowing as the corruption fraction increases. Figure 13 instead varies learning rate.
Zero training error on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian inputs. Permuted MNIST experiments measure continual-learning test accuracy.

The complete zero-to-total corruption range and a steadily increasing test-error trajectory toward chance cannot be established from the supplied flattened figures. Support for training-set fitting is qualitative rather than an exact zero-error measurement.
The named regularizers preventing fully random-label fitting, and generalization after their removal. NVRM uses a different regularization mechanism.
Separate learning trajectories for clean and corrupted examples establishing that shared patterns are learned first.

missing.what: Qualitative training-fit results across initial learning rates 0.1, 0.3, 1, and 3: SGD eventually memorizes nearly all noisy labels, while NVRM consistently reduces memorization. Extract these separately by optimizer and learning rate without inventing numerical accuracies.
missing.locator: Appendix E, discussion of large stochastic gradient noise; Figure 13 and caption, CIFAR-10 with 40% label noise.

record.verdict_notes: There are no existing rows to fix. Figures 3 and 10 are explicitly declared in rows_left_out, so they are not duplicated under missing. Flattened axes and legends cannot establish curve values. NVRM results qualify the optimizer scope of V4; they do not challenge random-label fitting under standard SGD or establish a failure of the specific regularizers named in V5.

versions.untested_parts: The study cites prior work on randomly labeled data but does not itself test completely random labels or fitting them without changes to training.
Does not compare training time for true versus random labels or report convergence time as a function of corrupted-label fraction.
Does not test shuffled-pixel or Gaussian-noise inputs.

Tests several nonzero corruption rates, but not the full range from none to all; does not report a numerical trajectory of test error steadily approaching chance. Figure 3 training-accuracy curves are figure-only, so no values are extracted.
Uses data augmentation and weight decay in general settings but does not compare removing them or test whether they prevent fitting random labels.
Does not measure the order in which real-label patterns and noisy labels are learned.

relationships.condition: ResNet-34 trained with SGD on partially corrupted CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 labels.
relationships.reason: Text accompanying Figures 3 and 10 states that SGD memorizes nearly all corrupted labels; Figure 13 reports eventual near-complete memorization across learning rates. This supports V4's training-fit component. Evidence is textual; no row ids were extracted.
relationships.display_finding: Nearly all corrupted labels were eventually memorized on both datasets across the tested learning rates.

relationships.condition: ResNet-34 trained with NVRM on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 with 10–40% asymmetric label noise.
relationships.reason: Figure 3's caption states that NVRM training error remains near the corruption rate, showing that near-perfect noisy-label fitting depends on the training objective. Evidence is textual; no row ids were extracted.
relationships.display_finding: Training error remained near the corruption rate rather than approaching zero.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
